prerequisites: Successful completion of the "Algorithms and Data Structures" module is required
Successful completion of the "Efficient Algorithms" module is recommended

learning_outcomes.text: Students can identify adequate parameterizations for hard computational problems
Students can develop efficient fixed-parameter algorithms and analyze their runtime
Students can design data reduction rules and analyze their effectiveness
Students can demonstrate the algorithmic difficulty of parameterized computational problems

syllabus_topics: Fundamental algorithmic techniques for parameterized algorithms: search tree algorithms, tree decompositions, iterative compression, color coding
Advanced algorithmic techniques for parameterized algorithms, for example, parameterization over lower bounds, inclusion-exclusion, representative sets

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercises
Oral examination (individual examination) or written examination

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50% of the points from the weekly exercises and orally present the solution to at least two exercises. Grading is based on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program. The examination performance consists of either an oral examination (individual) or a written examination.
bibliography: Cygan et al. Parameterized Algorithms. Springer Verlag, 2015.
Downey, Fellows: Fundamentals of Parameterized Complexity Theory. Springer Verlag 2013.
Niedermeier: Invitation to Fixed-Parameter Algorithms. Oxford University Press, 2006.
Flum, Grohe: Parameterized Complexity Theory. Springer Verlag, 2006.
